BEFORE  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UNNI KRISHNAN NAIR  HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE YARENJUNGLA LONGKUMER  ORDER Date : 04-02-2026 (N. U.K. Nair, J) Heard Mr. Sentiyanger, learned counsel for the applicant.
Also heard Ms. V. Zhimomi, learned Add. P.P. Nagaland appearing for the State.

By instituting the present interlocutory application, the applicant has prayed for condonation of delay of 6085 days in preferring the connected appeal assailing the judgment and order dated 17-02-2009 passed by the Page No.# 2/4 Addl. District Commissioner (Judicial), Nagaland in G.R.
Case No. 144/2025, convicting the applicant under Section 376/ 302/ IPC and sentencing the applicant to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life.

It is projected in the application that the applicant after his conviction under the above noted provisions of law, was not aware of his legal rights to prefer an appeal against his such conviction,
until he was informed of the same by the Para-legal Volunteers from the Nagaland State Legal Shri Pezazotuo Savino vs State Of Nagaland on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80133003/
1 Services Authority (NSLSA).

entities.text: Nagaland State Legal Shri Pezazotuo Savino vs State Of Nagaland
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is projected that he had, thereafter, written an application to the NSLSA for providing further legal assistance.
Thereafter, the present counsel was endorsed the case by the NSLSA to prefer the connected appeal along with the present interlocutory application.
Accordingly, upon completion of the requisite formalities, the present appeal was filed.

However, a delay of 6085 days occasioned in filing of the appeal and it is prayed that there is no willful and deliberate delay on the part of the applicant in preferring the connected appeal before this Court.

Ms. V. Zhimomi, learned Addl. P.P. Nagaland, on the other hand, submits that the appellant before the Trial Court was duly represented by a counsel and accordingly, the plea taken that he is ignorant about the provisions for filing of an appeal is not believable.
Under the circumstances, the learned Addl. P.P. submits that the delay in preferring the appeal may not be condoned.
We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and also perused the materials available on record.
The applicant has taken a plea of ignorance about the provision existing for filing of appeal before this Court against the order of his conviction and sentencing.
He has also projected that he had come to learn about the provisions for filing of an appeal after being apprised of the same by the Para-legal Volunteers of the NSLSA.
The said contention of the appellant is not seriously disputed by the learned Addl. P.P. Nagaland.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Dilip S. Dahanukar Vs. Page No.# 3/4 Kotak Mahindra Co. Ltd., reported in (2007) 6 SCC 528 has held that:
"12.

entities.text: Dilip S. Dahanukar Vs. Page No.# 3/4 Kotak Mahindra Co. Ltd., reported in (2007) 6 SCC 528
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An appeal is indisputably a statutory right and an offender who has been convicted is entitled to avail right of appeal which is provided for under Section 374 of the Code.
Right of appeal from a judgment of conviction affecting the liberty of a person keeping in view the expansive definition of Article 21 is also a fundamental right.
Right of appeal, thus, can neither be interfered with nor impaired, nor can it be subjected to any condition."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Abdul Ghafoor & Anr. Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2011) 14 SCC 465 has observed as follows:-
"3.

entities.text: Abdul Ghafoor & Anr. Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2011) 14 SCC 465
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We must, however, add that in cases of conviction and imposition of sentence or imprisonment, the court must show far greater indulgence and flexibility in applying the law of limitation than in any other kind of case.

A sentence of imprisonment relates to a person's right to personal liberty which is one of the most important rights available to an individual and, therefore, the court should be very reluctant to shut out a consideration of the case on merits on grounds of limitation or any other similar technicality."

Applying the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court noticed hereinabove as well as appreciating the contentions raised by the applicant for the purpose of condonation of delay in preferring the Shri Pezazotuo Savino vs State Of Nagaland on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80133003/
2 connected appeal, we have noticed that the applicant has been convicted for life and is presently under detention.

entities.text: Shri Pezazotuo Savino vs State Of Nagaland
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, we are of the considered view that the connected appeal as preferred by the applicant deserves to be examined on merit.

In view of the above and considering the contentions raised by the applicant in the present interlocutory application, we are of the view that the applicant has made out a case for condoning the delay.
Accordingly, the delay of 6085 days in preferring the connected appeal stands condoned.
Interlocutory application stands disposed of.
